title: Which months do I prune my rose?

common.applies_to: Hybrid Tea, Floribunda or Grandiflora bush rose in New Zealand; answer to a common question
common.preserved_uncertainty: Sources differ within the June to August window (C-1). One company says cooler places prune earlier, against the rest (C-2). Times for the north differ by up to a month (C-3). Christchurch is placed differently by two sources (C-4). Southern sources differ between late July and August (C-10). Two companies differ on whether to wait for the leaves to fall (C-12). No source draws a boundary for 'up north' or 'colder parts'. Months for the north, Northland, Auckland, Whanganui, Masterton, Canterbury, Christchurch and Dunedin each rest on one organisation or on garden companies. No New Zealand source names bud swell; three say to prune before growth starts.

content.heading: Which months do I prune my rose?

items.text: In New Zealand, the main winter pruning is done between June and August, depending on where you live. Months are only a guide, because frosts vary from year to year.
Prune later where it is colder: the north starts earlier than the south. One garden company says the opposite: that cooler places can prune earlier, once all the leaves have fallen.
Up north, one source says pruning starts around early July. Another says it can start a little before July. Months are only a guide.
In the colder parts of the South Island, pruning gets under way in August. In Dunedin, one source prunes in late July. Months are only a guide.
In Northland, one garden company says the end of July to early August is a good time to prune. Months are only a guide.
In Auckland, one garden service says to prune in July. One garden company says June to July, before the rose bursts into leaf, which can be as early as August in Auckland. Months are only a guide.
In Whanganui, one garden centre manager says roses are best pruned in July. Months are only a guide.
In Masterton, one garden company says to prune in July to August. Months are only a guide.

In Canterbury, one source says pruning can begin towards the end of July in milder parts and be completed there in August. Colder areas may prefer to wait until August, and colder inland districts prune once the worst frosts have passed. It says to finish winter pruning in September. Months are only a guide.
In Christchurch, one garden company says to leave pruning until late winter or early spring, after the last frost.

In Dunedin, one source prunes its modern roses in late July, when they are most dormant and the worst frosts are over. In a frosty spot that can mean waiting until mid-August. One garden company says June or July, and August if you are unsure. Months are only a guide.
Prune in winter, when the rose is dormant and not in active growth. In colder or frosty places, wait until the worst frosts have passed.
Don't leave pruning too late: prune before the rose bursts into growth.
Don't prune too early, because frost can damage the new growth that follows.

Two garden companies differ on a rose that still has its leaves or flowers in June. One says to wait until it is fully dormant, with no leaves left, which may mean pruning in July. The other says a rose can be pruned even if it is still flowering. Months are only a guide.
